blocks.en: "I have been crucified with Christ; it is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me; and the life which I now live in the flesh I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave Himself for me." — Galatians 2:20 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "Con Cristo estoy juntamente crucificado; y vivo, no ya yo, mas vive Cristo en mí; y lo que ahora vivo en la carne, lo vivo en la fe del Hijo de Dios, el cual me amó, y se entregó a sí mismo por mí." — Gálatas 2:20 (RVG)

blocks.en: Text: Galatians 2:11-21
blocks.es_reference: Texto: Gálatas 2:11-21 (RVG)

blocks.en: "Now when Peter had come to Antioch, I withstood him to his face, because he was to be blamed; for before certain men came from James, he would eat with the Gentiles; but when they came, he withdrew and separated himself, fearing those who were of the circumcision. And the rest of the Jews also played the hypocrite with him, so that even Barnabas was carried away with their hypocrisy. But when I saw that they were not straightforward about the truth of the gospel, I said to Peter before them all, 'If you, being a Jew, live in the manner of Gentiles and not as the Jews, why do you compel Gentiles to live as Jews?' We who are Jews by nature, and not sinners of the Gentiles, knowing that a man is not justified by the works of the law but by faith in Jesus Christ, even we have believed in Christ Jesus, that we might be justified by faith in Christ and not by the works of the law; for by the works of the law no flesh shall be justified. But if, while we seek to be justified by Christ, we ourselves also are found sinners, is Christ therefore a minister of sin? Certainly not! For if I build again those things which I destroyed, I make myself a transgressor. For I through the law died to the law that I might live to God. I have been crucified with Christ; it is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me; and the life which I now live in the flesh I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave Himself for me. I do not set aside the grace of God; for if righteousness comes through the law, then Christ died in vain." — Galatians 2:11-21 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "Pero cuando Pedro vino a Antioquía, le resistí cara a cara, porque era de condenar. Porque antes que viniesen unos de parte de Jacobo, comía con los gentiles; mas cuando vinieron, se retraía y se apartaba, teniendo miedo de los que eran de la circuncisión. Y a su simulación consentían también los otros judíos; de tal manera que aun Bernabé fue también arrastrado por la hipocresía de ellos. Mas cuando vi que no andaban rectamente conforme a la verdad del evangelio, dije a Pedro delante de todos: Si tú, siendo judío, vives como los gentiles y no como judío, ¿por qué constriñes a los gentiles a judaizar? Nosotros, judíos por naturaleza, y no pecadores de entre los gentiles, sabiendo que el hombre no es justificado por las obras de la ley, sino por la fe de Jesucristo, nosotros también hemos creído en Jesucristo, para que fuésemos justificados por la fe de Cristo, y no por las obras de la ley; por cuanto por las obras de la ley ninguna carne será justificada. Y si buscando nosotros ser justificados en Cristo, también nosotros somos hallados pecadores, ¿es por eso Cristo ministro de pecado? ¡En ninguna manera! Porque si las cosas que destruí, las mismas vuelvo a edificar, transgresor me hago. Porque yo por la ley soy muerto a la ley, para vivir para Dios. Con Cristo estoy juntamente crucificado; y vivo, no ya yo, mas vive Cristo en mí; y lo que ahora vivo en la carne, lo vivo en la fe del Hijo de Dios, el cual me amó, y se entregó a sí mismo por mí. No desecho la gracia de Dios; pues si por la ley fuese la justicia, entonces por demás murió Cristo." — Gálatas 2:11-21 (RVG)

blocks.en: A Public Clash at Antioch
blocks.es_reference: Un Choque Público en Antioquía

blocks.en: The first two chapters of Galatians are Paul's defense of the gospel he preaches. He has shown that this gospel did not come to him from men but by a revelation of Jesus Christ, and that the leaders at Jerusalem added nothing to it but recognized the grace given to him. Now Paul tells of a day when that gospel was tested in public — not by an enemy, but by a fellow apostle. The place is Antioch, the great mixed church of Jews and Gentiles, and the man Paul must oppose is Peter himself. Paul does not soften it: "I withstood him to his face, because he was to be blamed." This was no quarrel over preference. Paul saw the truth of the gospel itself at stake, and he would not let even an apostle cloud it.
blocks.es_reference: Los primeros dos capítulos de Gálatas son la defensa que Pablo hace del evangelio que predica. Ha mostrado que este evangelio no le vino de hombres sino por revelación de Jesucristo, y que los líderes en Jerusalén no le añadieron nada, sino que reconocieron la gracia que le había sido dada. Ahora Pablo cuenta de un día en que ese evangelio fue puesto a prueba en público — no por un enemigo, sino por un compañero apóstol. El lugar es Antioquía, la gran iglesia mixta de judíos y gentiles, y el hombre a quien Pablo debe oponerse es Pedro mismo. Pablo no lo suaviza: "le resistí cara a cara, porque era de condenar." No fue una disputa por preferencias. Pablo vio en juego la verdad misma del evangelio, y no permitiría que ni siquiera un apóstol la oscureciera.

blocks.en: Peter Withdraws
blocks.es_reference: Pedro se Retrae

blocks.en: When Peter first came to Antioch, he ate freely with the Gentile believers. To share a table in that world was to say, in the plainest way, "We are one family; you are fully my brothers." Peter's eating with the Gentiles was a living confession that in Christ the old wall between Jew and Gentile had come down. But then "certain men came from James" — men tied to the strict circumcision party in Jerusalem — and Peter's courage failed him. He drew back and separated himself from the Gentile believers, "fearing those who were of the circumcision." Notice carefully: Peter did not stand up and preach a false doctrine. His sin was one of conduct, of fear-driven behavior. Yet his withdrawal preached a sermon louder than words; it implied that the Gentile believers were second-class Christians unless they took up the marks of the Jewish law.
blocks.es_reference: Cuando Pedro llegó por primera vez a Antioquía, comía libremente con los creyentes gentiles. Compartir la mesa en aquel mundo era decir, de la manera más clara, "Somos una sola familia; ustedes son plenamente mis hermanos." El que Pedro comiera con los gentiles era una confesión viva de que en Cristo el viejo muro entre judío y gentil había caído. Pero entonces vinieron "unos de parte de Jacobo" — hombres ligados al estricto partido de la circuncisión en Jerusalén — y el valor de Pedro le falló. Se retrajo y se apartó de los creyentes gentiles, "teniendo miedo de los que eran de la circuncisión." Note con cuidado: Pedro no se levantó a predicar una falsa doctrina. Su pecado fue de conducta, un comportamiento movido por el miedo. Sin embargo, su retraimiento predicó un sermón más fuerte que las palabras; daba a entender que los creyentes gentiles eran cristianos de segunda clase a menos que tomaran las marcas de la ley judía.

blocks.en: The Spread of Hypocrisy
blocks.es_reference: El Contagio de la Hipocresía

blocks.en: Sin in a leader is never a private thing. "And the rest of the Jews also played the hypocrite with him, so that even Barnabas was carried away with their hypocrisy." The word hypocrite means an actor, one who wears a mask — for these men knew better, yet acted against what they knew. And the contagion did not stop with the weak; it swept up Barnabas, the large-hearted man who had first vouched for Paul and traveled with him preaching to the Gentiles. If even Barnabas could be carried away, none of us should imagine ourselves above such pressure. This is how compromise works: one respected man flinches, a crowd follows, and soon the whole church is acting out a lie.
blocks.es_reference: El pecado en un líder nunca es cosa privada. "Y a su simulación consentían también los otros judíos; de tal manera que aun Bernabé fue también arrastrado por la hipocresía de ellos." La palabra hipócrita significa un actor, uno que lleva una máscara — pues estos hombres sabían lo correcto, y sin embargo actuaron contra lo que sabían. Y el contagio no se detuvo en los débiles; arrastró a Bernabé, el hombre de gran corazón que primero había respondido por Pablo y viajado con él predicando a los gentiles. Si aun Bernabé pudo ser arrastrado, ninguno de nosotros debe imaginarse por encima de tal presión. Así obra el compromiso: un hombre respetado vacila, una multitud le sigue, y pronto toda la iglesia está representando una mentira.

blocks.en: A note on the setting. In the ancient world, to eat at a person's table was a sign of full acceptance and fellowship. For a Jew to share a meal with Gentiles was to treat them as equals before God. The men "from James" belonged to the circumcision party — believers who still insisted that Gentiles must be circumcised and keep the law of Moses to be true members of God's people. By drawing back, Peter sided in practice with their error, even though he knew the gospel better.
blocks.es_reference: Una nota sobre el contexto. En el mundo antiguo, comer a la mesa de una persona era señal de plena aceptación y comunión. Que un judío compartiera una comida con gentiles era tratarlos como iguales delante de Dios. Los hombres "de parte de Jacobo" pertenecían al partido de la circuncisión — creyentes que aún insistían en que los gentiles debían circuncidarse y guardar la ley de Moisés para ser verdaderos miembros del pueblo de Dios. Al retraerse, Pedro se puso en la práctica del lado de su error, aunque conocía mejor el evangelio.

blocks.en: Withstood to His Face
blocks.es_reference: Resistido Cara a Cara

blocks.en: Paul saw what was happening and would not keep silent. "When I saw that they were not straightforward about the truth of the gospel, I said to Peter before them all..." Because the error was public, the rebuke had to be public. Paul put a single piercing question to Peter: "If you, being a Jew, live in the manner of Gentiles and not as the Jews, why do you compel Gentiles to live as Jews?" The inconsistency was glaring. Peter himself had been living in gospel freedom, eating with Gentiles; now, by his withdrawal, he was pressing those same Gentiles to take up the Jewish law in order to be accepted. Paul rebuked the apostle, but he did it for the apostle's good and for the truth's sake, and we have no record that Peter resented it. The two remained brothers; Peter would later call Paul "our beloved brother" (2 Peter 3:15).
blocks.es_reference: Pablo vio lo que sucedía y no quiso callar. "cuando vi que no andaban rectamente conforme a la verdad del evangelio, dije a Pedro delante de todos..." Porque el error era público, la reprensión tuvo que ser pública. Pablo puso a Pedro una sola pregunta penetrante: "Si tú, siendo judío, vives como los gentiles y no como judío, ¿por qué constriñes a los gentiles a judaizar?" La incoherencia era evidente. El mismo Pedro había estado viviendo en la libertad del evangelio, comiendo con gentiles; ahora, por su retraimiento, presionaba a esos mismos gentiles a tomar la ley judía para ser aceptados. Pablo reprendió al apóstol, pero lo hizo por el bien del apóstol y por causa de la verdad, y no hay registro de que Pedro lo resintiera. Los dos siguieron siendo hermanos; Pedro más tarde llamaría a Pablo "nuestro amado hermano" (2 Pedro 3:15).

blocks.en: Justified by Faith, Not by Works of the Law
blocks.es_reference: Justificados por la Fe, No por las Obras de la Ley

blocks.en: From the incident Paul rises to the doctrine beneath it. "We who are Jews by nature, and not sinners of the Gentiles, knowing that a man is not justified by the works of the law but by faith in Jesus Christ..." To justify is a courtroom word; it means to declare a person righteous, to acquit. The great question of the gospel is how a guilty sinner can be declared righteous before a holy God. Paul gives the answer plainly: not by the works of the law, but by faith in Jesus Christ. "Even we," Paul says — even we Jews, who had the law and the covenants — had to come the same way, believing in Christ to be justified by faith and not by works. And he ends the verse with a hammer-blow: "by the works of the law no flesh shall be justified." No one, Jew or Gentile, has ever been or ever will be made right with God by law-keeping.
blocks.es_reference: Del incidente Pablo se eleva a la doctrina que está debajo. "Nosotros, judíos por naturaleza, y no pecadores de entre los gentiles, sabiendo que el hombre no es justificado por las obras de la ley, sino por la fe de Jesucristo..." Justificar es una palabra de tribunal; significa declarar justa a una persona, absolverla. La gran pregunta del evangelio es cómo un pecador culpable puede ser declarado justo delante de un Dios santo. Pablo da la respuesta con claridad: no por las obras de la ley, sino por la fe de Jesucristo. "Nosotros también," dice Pablo — aun nosotros los judíos, que teníamos la ley y los pactos — tuvimos que venir de la misma manera, creyendo en Cristo para ser justificados por la fe y no por las obras. Y cierra el versículo con un golpe de martillo: "por las obras de la ley ninguna carne será justificada." Nadie, judío o gentil, ha sido jamás ni será jamás hecho justo delante de Dios por guardar la ley.

blocks.en: "The works of the law." By this phrase Paul means everything the law of Moses requires — its commands, its ceremonies, and the badges the Judaizers prized most, such as circumcision. His point is sweeping: no part of law-keeping, and no human effort of any kind, can make a sinner right with God. Justification is God's free gift, received by faith in Christ alone.
blocks.es_reference: "Las obras de la ley." Con esta frase Pablo quiere decir todo lo que la ley de Moisés requiere — sus mandamientos, sus ceremonias, y las insignias que los judaizantes más apreciaban, como la circuncisión. Su punto es amplio: ninguna parte del cumplimiento de la ley, ni esfuerzo humano alguno, puede hacer justo a un pecador delante de Dios. La justificación es el don gratuito de Dios, recibido por la fe en Cristo solamente.

blocks.en: Is Christ a Minister of Sin?
blocks.es_reference: ¿Es Cristo Ministro de Pecado?

blocks.en: Paul now answers an objection. If we leave the law behind and seek to be justified in Christ alone, and we are still found to be sinners, does that make Christ a promoter of sin — as though grace were a license to live as we please? Paul's reply is sharp: "Certainly not!" The fault is never in Christ or in His grace. Then he turns the charge around: "For if I build again those things which I destroyed, I make myself a transgressor." It is not faith that makes a man a transgressor; it is returning to the law as a way of salvation after the gospel has torn it down. To rebuild that old system is to step backward into condemnation.
blocks.es_reference: Pablo ahora responde a una objeción. Si dejamos atrás la ley y buscamos ser justificados en Cristo solamente, y aun así somos hallados pecadores, ¿hace eso de Cristo un promotor del pecado — como si la gracia fuera licencia para vivir como nos plazca? La respuesta de Pablo es tajante: "¡En ninguna manera!" La culpa nunca está en Cristo ni en su gracia. Luego vuelve la acusación al revés: "si las cosas que destruí, las mismas vuelvo a edificar, transgresor me hago." No es la fe lo que hace a un hombre transgresor; es volver a la ley como camino de salvación después de que el evangelio la ha derribado. Volver a edificar aquel viejo sistema es retroceder a la condenación.

blocks.en: Crucified with Christ
blocks.es_reference: Con Cristo Juntamente Crucificado

blocks.en: Now Paul speaks from the depths of his own heart. "For I through the law died to the law that I might live to God." The law itself, by condemning him, drove him out of every hope in himself and to Christ; he died to the law as a way of life that he might truly live to God. Then comes one of the most precious verses in all of Scripture: "I have been crucified with Christ; it is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me; and the life which I now live in the flesh I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave Himself for me." The old self that tried to earn God's favor was nailed to the cross with Jesus. The life Paul now lives is the life of Christ in him, received and lived out by faith. And see how personal it becomes: the Son of God "loved me and gave Himself for me." The gospel is not only a doctrine about the many; it is a love that reaches down to the single believer.
blocks.es_reference: Ahora Pablo habla desde lo profundo de su propio corazón. "Porque yo por la ley soy muerto a la ley, para vivir para Dios." La ley misma, al condenarlo, lo sacó de toda esperanza en sí mismo y lo llevó a Cristo; murió a la ley como modo de vida para poder de veras vivir para Dios. Luego viene uno de los versículos más preciosos de toda la Escritura: "Con Cristo estoy juntamente crucificado; y vivo, no ya yo, mas vive Cristo en mí; y lo que ahora vivo en la carne, lo vivo en la fe del Hijo de Dios, el cual me amó, y se entregó a sí mismo por mí." El viejo yo que trataba de ganar el favor de Dios fue clavado en la cruz con Jesús. La vida que Pablo ahora vive es la vida de Cristo en él, recibida y vivida por la fe. Y vea cuán personal se vuelve: el Hijo de Dios "me amó, y se entregó a sí mismo por mí." El evangelio no es solo una doctrina acerca de muchos; es un amor que desciende hasta el creyente individual.

blocks.en: To add anything to the finished work of Christ is not to honor the law but to empty the cross.
blocks.es_reference: Añadir cualquier cosa a la obra consumada de Cristo no es honrar la ley sino vaciar la cruz.

blocks.en: If Righteousness Came by the Law
blocks.es_reference: Si la Justicia Fuese por la Ley

blocks.en: All that Paul has said gathers into the verse that gives this unit its name: "I do not set aside the grace of God; for if righteousness comes through the law, then Christ died in vain." Here is the logic in its starkest form. Grace and law-righteousness cannot both be the ground of our standing with God; to add the law as a means of being justified is to set grace aside. And if a person could be made righteous by keeping the law, then the cross was needless and Christ died for nothing. To add anything to the finished work of Christ is not to honor the law but to empty the cross. Paul will not do it. He will not set aside the grace of God.
blocks.es_reference: Todo lo que Pablo ha dicho se reúne en el versículo que da nombre a esta unidad: "No desecho la gracia de Dios; pues si por la ley fuese la justicia, entonces por demás murió Cristo." Aquí está la lógica en su forma más cruda. La gracia y la justicia por la ley no pueden ser ambas el fundamento de nuestra posición delante de Dios; añadir la ley como medio de ser justificados es desechar la gracia. Y si una persona pudiera ser hecha justa guardando la ley, entonces la cruz era innecesaria y Cristo murió por nada. Añadir cualquier cosa a la obra consumada de Cristo no es honrar la ley sino vaciar la cruz. Pablo no lo hará. No desechará la gracia de Dios.

blocks.en: A Note on Paul's Words
blocks.es_reference: Una Nota sobre las Palabras de Pablo

blocks.en: Careful readers have long asked where Paul's speech to Peter ends and his teaching to the Galatians begins — whether verses 15 through 21 are still spoken to Peter at Antioch or are Paul now reasoning directly with his readers. Sincere students differ, and the passage does not settle the matter for us. Happily, the truth is the same either way: a sinner is justified before God by faith in Christ, not by the works of the law. Whether first spoken to an apostle or written to a struggling church, it is the word we all must hear.
blocks.es_reference: Los lectores cuidadosos han preguntado desde antiguo dónde termina el discurso de Pablo a Pedro y dónde comienza su enseñanza a los gálatas — si los versículos 15 al 21 todavía se dirigen a Pedro en Antioquía o si Pablo ahora razona directamente con sus lectores. Estudiantes sinceros difieren, y el pasaje no nos lo resuelve. Felizmente, la verdad es la misma en ambos casos: el pecador es justificado delante de Dios por la fe en Cristo, no por las obras de la ley. Sea dicho primero a un apóstol o escrito a una iglesia que lucha, es la palabra que todos debemos oír.

blocks.en: The Heart of the Matter
blocks.es_reference: El Corazón del Asunto

blocks.en: The clash at Antioch was not really about food or tables; it was about whether the gospel is enough. Peter, by drawing back in fear, had let his conduct deny what his lips confessed — that we are saved by grace through faith in Christ alone. Paul saw that to add the law to the gospel, even by a quiet withdrawal, is to lose the gospel altogether. So he teaches us that justification is by faith, that the believer has died with Christ and now lives by Christ, and that to seek righteousness by the law is to make the cross meaningless. This presses upon us not only what we believe but how we live and how we treat one another in the church. A people justified by grace must walk by grace, and must never set aside the grace of God.
blocks.es_reference: El choque en Antioquía no era en realidad acerca de comida ni de mesas; era acerca de si el evangelio basta. Pedro, al retraerse por miedo, había dejado que su conducta negara lo que sus labios confesaban — que somos salvos por gracia mediante la fe en Cristo solamente. Pablo vio que añadir la ley al evangelio, aun por un callado retraimiento, es perder el evangelio por completo. Así que nos enseña que la justificación es por la fe, que el creyente ha muerto con Cristo y ahora vive por Cristo, y que buscar la justicia por la ley es hacer la cruz sin sentido. Esto nos urge no solo lo que creemos sino cómo vivimos y cómo nos tratamos unos a otros en la iglesia. Un pueblo justificado por gracia debe andar por gracia, y nunca debe desechar la gracia de Dios.

blocks.en: "I do not set aside the grace of God; for if righteousness comes through the law, then Christ died in vain." — Galatians 2:21 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "No desecho la gracia de Dios; pues si por la ley fuese la justicia, entonces por demás murió Cristo." — Gálatas 2:21 (RVG)

sa.prompt: Describe the incident at Antioch: what did Peter do, and why did Paul withstand him to his face?
sa.model: When Peter first came to Antioch he ate freely with the Gentile believers, showing that in Christ Jew and Gentile are one family. But when certain men came from James, Peter drew back and separated himself out of fear, fearing those of the circumcision. His sin was not false teaching but cowardly conduct, for his withdrawal implied that Gentile believers were second-class unless they kept the law. The rest of the Jews joined his hypocrisy, and even Barnabas was carried away. Paul saw that this behavior denied the truth of the gospel, so he rebuked Peter publicly, to his face. By living like a Gentile and then pulling away, Peter was in effect compelling Gentiles to live as Jews. Paul withstood him not out of rivalry but to guard the gospel itself.

sa.prompt: Explain how hypocrisy spreads, and why it mattered that 'even Barnabas' was carried away.
sa.model: Peter's failure shows how quickly hypocrisy spreads when a respected leader sets a bad example. The word hypocrite means an actor wearing a mask, for these men knew the truth of the gospel yet acted against it out of fear. Peter's compromise did not stay with him; the other Jewish believers followed, and even Barnabas was carried away. Barnabas was no weakling; he had vouched for Paul and labored among the Gentiles, yet he too was swept along. This warns us that no one is beyond such pressure. When one leader flinches, a whole congregation can be carried into a lie. The danger is not always open false teaching; often it is a quiet compromise of conduct that betrays the gospel just as surely. We must guard the truth not only in what we say but in how we act.

sa.prompt: What does it mean to be 'justified,' and how does Paul say a person is justified?
sa.model: To justify is a courtroom word that means to declare a person righteous, to acquit. The great question of the gospel is how a guilty sinner can be declared righteous before a holy God. Paul answers that a man is not justified by the works of the law but by faith in Jesus Christ. Even Jewish believers, who had the law, had to be justified the same way, by faith and not by works, for by the works of the law no flesh shall be justified. This righteousness is not earned; it is God's free gift of grace, received by trusting in Christ. So justification rests entirely on Christ and is grasped by faith alone. No human effort and no keeping of the law can make a sinner right with God; only faith in Christ can.

sa.prompt: Even Jewish believers ('we who are Jews by nature') had to be justified by faith. Why is this significant for the Gentile question at Antioch?
sa.model: Paul says, 'We who are Jews by nature, and not sinners of the Gentiles,' yet even these Jews had to be justified by faith in Christ. This is the crushing answer to the Judaizers at Antioch. If the Jews themselves, who possessed the law, could not be justified by it but only by faith, then there is no higher ground for them to stand on over the Gentiles. Jew and Gentile alike come as sinners and are made right with God on equal footing, through faith in Christ and not by the works of the law. This is why Peter's withdrawal was so wrong: it treated the Gentile believers as second-class, when in truth they stood on the very same ground as Jewish believers. All are saved by grace through faith in Christ.

sa.prompt: The objection arises: is Christ then 'a minister of sin'? State the objection and Paul's answer, including verse 18.
sa.model: Paul anticipates an objection: if we seek to be justified in Christ alone and are still found to be sinners, does that make Christ a minister of sin, as though grace were a license to sin? His answer is emphatic: certainly not! The fault is never in Christ or in His grace. Then Paul turns it around. He says that if he were to build again the very things he destroyed, namely the law as a way of salvation, he would only prove himself a transgressor. The man who returns to law-keeping after the gospel has torn it down does not become more holy; he steps back into condemnation. So it is not faith in Christ that makes a sinner a transgressor, but the attempt to rebuild what Christ has abolished.

sa.prompt: Explain the meaning of verse 20, 'I have been crucified with Christ...'
sa.model: In one of the most precious verses of Scripture Paul says he has been crucified with Christ. The old self that tried to earn God's favor was nailed to the cross with Jesus, so that it is no longer I who live, but Christ who lives in me. The life Paul now has in the flesh he lives by faith in the Son of God. Notice three things. First, the believer is united with Christ in His death; the self that trusted in the law is crucified. Second, the new life is the life of Christ within him, not a self-powered effort. Third, this life is received and lived by faith. And see how personal it is: the Son of God loved me and gave Himself for me. The gospel reaches down in love to each single believer.

sa.prompt: Explain the paradox of verse 19: 'I through the law died to the law that I might live to God.'
sa.model: Paul says, 'For I through the law died to the law that I might live to God.' This is a striking paradox. The law itself, by condemning him and showing him he could never keep it, drove him out of all hope in himself and pointed him to Christ. So he died to the law as a way of being right with God, in order that he might truly live to God by faith. He did not abandon obedience; rather, he stopped trusting the law to save him. The gospel does not make us lawless; it kills our false confidence in law-keeping so that we may live a new life to God, resting on grace. This is the same gospel that Peter's withdrawal had obscured, for to go back to the law is to leave the grace of God behind.

sa.prompt: Verse 21 gives the unit its name. Explain Paul's logic: why does seeking righteousness by the law set aside grace and empty the cross?
sa.model: The unit's title comes from this verse: 'I do not set aside the grace of God; for if righteousness comes through the law, then Christ died in vain.' Paul's logic is stark. Grace and law-righteousness cannot both be the ground of our standing with God. To add the law as a means of being justified is to set the grace of God aside. And the conclusion is devastating: if a person could be made righteous by keeping the law, then the cross was unnecessary and Christ died for nothing. To add anything to the finished work of Christ does not honor the law; it empties the cross of meaning. Paul refuses to do this. He will not set aside the grace of God, because the grace shown at the cross is the only ground on which any sinner can be made righteous.

sa.prompt: This passage teaches that the gospel must shape not only what we confess but how we live and treat one another. Explain, using Peter's failure of conduct.
sa.model: This passage teaches that the gospel must shape not only what we confess but how we live. Peter never denied the gospel with his lips; his failure was one of conduct. By withdrawing from the Gentiles he acted out a lie, treating fellow believers as unequal when in Christ they stood on equal ground. His hypocrisy obscured the truth of the gospel just as surely as false teaching would have. The lesson for us is that grace must govern our behavior and our relationships in the church. A people justified by faith must welcome one another as equals, for all alike are saved by grace. To act in a way that divides believers, or that suggests some are second-class, betrays the very gospel we claim to believe. Sound doctrine and loving, consistent conduct must go together.

sa.prompt: Summarize the central truth of Unit 3: what does Galatians 2:11-21 teach about how a sinner is made right with God?
sa.model: The central truth of Unit 3 is that a sinner is justified before God by faith in Christ alone, not by the works of the law. At Antioch this truth was threatened when Peter, by his conduct, implied that Gentiles must keep the law to be accepted. Paul defended the gospel by teaching that no flesh is justified by law-keeping; even Jewish believers are justified by faith. The believer has been crucified with Christ and now lives by faith in the Son of God who loved him. And Paul will not set aside the grace of God, for if righteousness came through the law, Christ died in vain. In short, salvation is by grace through faith in Christ, apart from works, and this gospel must govern both our belief and our behavior toward one another.
